3.text:
PART 3
[8 marks]
Questions 19 to 26
Read the passage carefully and choose the best answer A, B, C or D. For each question, mark
your answer on the answer sheet.
It was the first day of school, and Alex sat alone in the cafeteria, nervously picking at
his sandwich. Having recently moved to a new town, everything around him felt strange and
overwhelming. The students nearby were chatting and laughing comfortably with their friends,
creating an atmosphere of excitement and ease that Alex could not yet share. He was a stranger
to everyone around him and the sense of isolation made him wish he were anywhere else.
Just as he was about to stand up and leave, a warm voice interrupted his thoughts. "Hey,
you're new here, right?" Alex looked up and saw a boy with a friendly smile standing in front of
him. "I'm Daniel. Do you want to sit with us?" he offered.
A wave of relief washed over Alex. He smiled and nodded, grateful for the kind gesture. He
followed Daniel to a nearby table where a small group of students welcomed him with genuine
warmth. From that moment onward, a meaningful friendship began to blossom between Alex
and Daniel.
As they spent more time together, they discovered that they had a lot in common. Both were
passionate about football, enjoyed playing video games and shared a similar sense of humour.
While Alex aspired to become a doctor, driven by a desire to help others, Daniel dreamed of
becoming a professional artist. Although their future goals were different, their shared interests
and mutual support formed a solid foundation for their friendship.
In the weeks that followed, the two became inseparable. They walked home from
school together, shared their lunches and helped each other with homework. Whenever Alex
felt discouraged or struggled with his schoolwork, Daniel was always there to motivate him.
Likewise, when Daniel faced challenges at home, Alex provided a listening ear and comforting
advice.
One day, the school announced that a football tournament would be held in two weeks, and
both friends eagerly signed up. Determined to perform well, they began practising every evening
after school, working hard to improve their teamwork and skills. They dreamed of winning the
tournament together.
However, a week before the match, Alex twisted his ankle during a training session. The
doctor advised him to rest for at least two weeks, which meant he wouldn't be able to play in the
tournament. As if that wasn't enough, he also caught the flu a few days later and had to miss
several days of school. Though disappointed, Alex chose to make the best of the situation and
used his time at home to focus on preparing for the upcoming exams.
Meanwhile, Daniel continued practising with the team. During one practice session, he
noticed Alex sitting quietly on the bench, watching with a mixture of pride and sadness. Daniel
approached him and said, "You're still part of the team, Alex. We need your support, even if you
can't play"
On the day of the tournament, Alex cheered enthusiastically from the sidelines. He watched
with admiration as Daniel gave his best performance on the field. In the final match, Daniel
scored two goals, leading their team to a well-earned victory. As soon as the final whistle blew
and the trophy was awarded, Daniel rushed over to Alex.

"This is for both of us," he said, handing him the trophy with a smile. Later, he also invited
Alex to the team's victory celebration, making sure that his friend still felt included
That touching gesture reminded Alex that true friendship goes beyond shared hobbies
or good times -- it is built on loyalty, understanding and support through both triumphs and
setbacks.
Years later, at their graduation ceremony, Alex and Daniel stood side by side, reflecting on
everything they had been through together. Life would soon take them on different paths, but
one thing remained certain: the bond they had formed would stand the test of time.

PART 4
[6 marks]
Questions 27 to 32
You are going to read an article on health benefits of e-sports for teenagers. Six sentences
have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A to H the one which fits
each gap (27 to 32). There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. Mark your
answers on the answer sheet.
Health Benefits of E-sports for Teenagers
E-sports, or competitive video gaming, has become increasingly popular among
teenagers around the world. While some people believe gaming only has negative effects,
many studies and personal experiences show that e-sports can offer several health benefits,
especially for teenagers. (27) It encourages healthy habits when combined with
regular exercise, proper rest and time management.
One of the main health benefits of e-sports is the improvement of thinking skills.
(28) L
As a result, players can strengthen their focus, memory and concentration
skills that are also useful in school and daily life.
Another benefit is emotional health. (29)L
By playing games they enjoy, they
can improve their mood and reduce anxiety. When they achieve goals in a game, they
experience a sense of success and satisfaction, which helps build confidence. (30)
Too much screen time can lead to eye strain, poor posture and difficulty concentrating on
schoolwork.
E-sports also encourages social interaction and teamwork. Many games are played in
teams, where players must communicate, plan and cooperate to win. (31)] Through
online platforms, teenagers can make new friends who share the same interests, helping
them feel more connected and less isolated.
(32) For example, many professional e-sports players follow fitness programs
to stay healthy and perform better. Teenagers can learn from this and include exercise,
good sleep and proper nutrition in their daily lives.
In conclusion, when practiced responsibly, e-sports can offer many health benefits
for teenagers. It helps them grow mentally, emotionally and socially. Parents and teachers
can support this interest by encouraging healthy limits and balance.

A The popularity of some e-sports titles depends on game updates.
B After a long day at school, playing games can help teenagers relax and feel better
physically.
C Although e-sports mostly involves sitting, it can still lead to better physical habits when
balanced with healthy routines.
D However, it's important for teens to take regular breaks and avoid long gaming hours to
prevent fatigue or burnout.
E This helps teenagers build communication skills and learn how to work with others,
even if their teammates are in different countries.
F E-sports can be a great way for teenagers to release stress and relax after a long day
at school.
G When practiced in a balanced and responsible way, e-sports can support mental, social
and even physical well-being.
H Teenagers who play strategy-based games develop better decision-making abilities,
faster reaction times and improved problem-solving skills.

How Teenagers Make Money?
A - Aiman, 16
Sometimes I help my neighbours to wash their cars, cut the grass or carry heavy things.
It does not pay much, but every little bit helps. I save most of the money for things I
really want, like video games or sports equipment. Doing these small jobs also teaches me
responsibility and hard work. I feel proud knowing that I'm earning money on my own.
B - Adelina, 17
I work part-time at a bakery on weekends. It's quite tiring because I have to wake up early,
but I enjoy it. I learn a lot about customer service and baking too. The best part is getting
paid every month, which gives me more independence. I also use the money to buy things
I need and save for the future.
C- Jason, 15
I sell my old books and clothes online. I use apps to post pictures and chat with buyers. It's
simple and I don't need to spend any money to get started. It also helps me clear my room
and be more organised. I feel happy knowing my items can be reused by others instead of
being thrown away.
D - Ainaa, 16
I save money from my school pocket money. I try not to buy snacks every, day and bring
food from home. After a few months, I usually have enough to buy something nice. Saving
is slow, but I like knowing I earned.it myself. It also teaches me to be more disciplined and
think carefully before spending.
E - Vincent, 17
My cousin and I run a small online business. We design and sell phone cases which are
handmade. We started with just a few designs, but now we have many customers. It's fun
and creative and we both learn about business at the same time. We also handle customer
service, manage orders and promote our products through social media platforms.
F - Sarah, 16
I tutor younger kids in English and Math. I only teach two students, but it allows me to
revise what I've learned as well. Their parents pay me weekly. It feels good to help someone
and earn money at the same time. I also learn to be more patient, responsible and better at
explaining things in a simple way.
